subject: Re: ETV PROD | Pod Restart Alert | vr-scheduler - Observations
description: Hi @Diwash Sanjel <diwash.sanjel@tothenew.com> Could you please share your inputs over the email for the shared points so that we can proceed further? Warm Regards, *Yash Chabra* Senior Executive - Service Delivery M: +91-7905643740 | <https://www.linkedin.com/company/tothenew> On Tue, Feb 3, 2026 at 8:12 PM Gaurav Kumar Dwivedi < gaurav.dwivedi1@tothenew.com> wrote: > Hi Diwash, > > We investigated the recent restart of the *vr-scheduler* pod and > performed a detailed correlation between the application logs and the > MongoDB replica set logs for the same time window. Below are the > consolidated findings and technical root cause. > *Incident Time (UTC / IST)* > > > * - UTC: 31 Jan 21:59:00- IST: 01 Feb 03:29:00* > > This is the exact time when the Quartz scheduler thread encountered a > runtime failure and the pod was subsequently restarted by Kubernetes. > *Observed Error in Application Logs* > > The Quartz MongoDB job store reported the following error repeatedly: > > *com.mongodb.MongoWriteConcernException: waiting for replication timed out* > > This was followed by: > > *CheckinTask : Node could not check-in: waiting for replication timed out > QuartzSchedulerThread : Runtime error occurred in main trigger firing loop > Scheduler shutting down* > > After this, Quartz performed a graceful shutdown by design, and Kubernetes > restarted the container. > > Additionally, multiple errors of the form below were observed: > > *E11000 duplicate key error collection: vr_scheduler__locks > Trigger hasn't expired yet* > > These are not the root issue but a side effect of the write concern > failure, explained below. > *What Quartz Was Doing at That Time* > > Quartz (using the MongoDB job store) continuously performs: > > - Insert/update of trigger locks in *vr_scheduler__locks* > - Scheduler check-in updates > - Trigger state replace operations > > All of these operations use *majority write concern*. > > This means MongoDB must confirm replication of the write to a majority of > replica set members before acknowledging success. > *What Happened Inside MongoDB at the Same Time* > > MongoDB logs for the same timeframe show clear evidence of: > > - Heavy read load on secondaries (due to secondaryPreferred traffic) > - Oplog maintenance bursts > - Interrupted operations and client reconnection storms > - Secondaries busy serving reads instead of applying oplog entries > - Signs of replication catch-up and recovery immediately after the > incident window > > This is a classic MongoDB *replication lag + flow control* scenario. > > When secondaries lag behind replication, MongoDB enables *Flow Control* > on the primary. During this state: > > The primary intentionally delays or withholds acknowledgements for > majority writes until secondaries catch up. > > This directly explains why Quartz received: > > *waiting for replication timed out* > > MongoDB was not able to confirm replication to majority in the configured > timeout. > *Why Duplicate Key Errors Appeared* > > Sequence of events: > > 1. Quartz attempted to insert a lock document. > 2. Mongo primarily accepted the write, but replication confirmation > did not happen in time. > 3. Quartz treated this as a failure and retried the insert. > 4. Mongo responded with a duplicate key, because the document already > existed on primary. > > This confirms that writes were reaching primary but replication was > delayed. > *Why Quartz Shut Down and Pod Restarted* > > Quartz has a built-in cluster safety mechanism. > > When the scheduler *cannot perform a check-in* with the job store, it > assumes the cluster state is unsafe and intentionally shuts itself down. > > This is expected behavior of Quartz Mongo job store under write concern > failure. > > Kubernetes simply restarted the container after Quartz exited. > *Root Cause* > > MongoDB replica set experienced replication lag due to heavy read pressure > on secondaries. This triggered MongoDB flow control on the primary, > preventing majority write acknowledgements within the configured timeout. > Quartz Mongo job store operations failed with write concern timeout, > causing Quartz to self-terminate and resulting in pod restart. > > This is an infrastructure-level behavior, not an application defect. > *Why This Can Reoccur* > > Current architecture has: > > - Quartz using majority write concern for locks and check-ins > - High usage of secondaryPreferred reads by applications/exporters > - Secondaries serving reads heavily, impacting replication speed > > Under load, this condition can repeat. > *Recommended Permanent Fixes*1. Reduce Quartz Write Concern (Most > Important) > Quartz locks and check-ins do not require majority durability. > Configure Quartz Mongo options to use: > writeConcern = w1 > This prevents Quartz from depending on replica acknowledgement.2. Review > and Reduce Heavy secondaryPreferred Read Traffic > Move heavy readers/exporters to primary or add additional secondaries.3. > Increase Oplog Size > Helps secondaries catch up faster and reduces lag scenarios.4. Add > Monitoring/Alerts for Replication Lag > Set alerts on replication delay before it impacts applications. > > The pod restart was a direct consequence of MongoDB replication lag and > write concern timeout affecting Quartz scheduler’s cluster check-in > mechanism. This is a known sensitivity of Quartz Mongo job stores under > replica lag conditions. > > Please let me know if we can proceed with the Quartz configuration change > and Mongo replica set tuning. > > > > *Warm Regards,* > > *Gaurav Kumar Dwivedi* > > *Senior Cloud Engineer* > > > On Mon, Feb 2, 2026 at 5:44 PM Yash Chabra <yash.chabra@tothenew.com> > wrote: > >> Adding the BCT team and @Shishupal Shakya <shishupal.shakya@tothenew.com> >> to this thread for further investigation. >> >> Warm Regards, >> >> *Yash Chabra* >> >> Senior Executive - Service Delivery >> >> M: +91-7905643740 | <https://www.linkedin.com/company/tothenew> >> >> >> >> On Sun, Feb 1, 2026 at 7:09 AM Sankalp Batra <sankalp.batra@tothenew.com> >> wrote: >> >>> +Shared OTT SRE Team <shared-ott-sreteam@tothenew.com> >>> >>> Warm Regards, >>> >>> Sankalp Batra >>> >>> Cloud Engineer >>> >>> M: +91-9625431079 >>> >>> www.tothenew.com | <https://www.linkedin.com/company/tothenew> >>> >>> >>> >>> >>> On Sun, Feb 1, 2026 at 4:31 AM Sankalp Batra <sankalp.batra@tothenew.com> >>> wrote: >>> >>>> Hi Diwash, >>>> >>>> We received the alert for the *Pod restart *of service *vr-scheduler*. >>>> >>>> *Alert Name: [FIRING:1] vr-scheduler | High Pod Restart Count – >>>> Kubernetes Alert* >>>> >>>> Upon checking the namespace, we observed that *both vr-scheduler pods >>>> were restarted around the same time*: >>>> >>>> Pods Status: >>>> [image: image.png] >>>> >>>> - >>>> >>>> vr-scheduler-5c9c7fcf4b-fj48g – restarted ~43 minutes ago >>>> - >>>> >>>> vr-scheduler-5c9c7fcf4b-l7sm4 – restarted ~42 minutes ago >>>> >>>> *Currently, both pods are in the Running (2/2) state.* >>>> >>>> During log review around the restart window, we noticed multiple >>>> repeated entries similar to the following: >>>> >>>> *Error Logs: >>>> >>>> duplicate key error collection: prod_content.vr_scheduler_locks >>>> index: keyGroup_1_keyName_1_type_1 dup key >>>> Failed to lock trigger ... reason: WriteError(code=11000) >>>> org.quartz.mongodb.LockManager >>>> QuartzSchedulerThread >>>> *[image: image.png] >>>> >>>> >>>> *These log entries were seen multiple times across the restart period.* >>>> >>>> In addition, based on monitoring dashboards around the same time window (~03:29–03:30): >>>> >>>> -
